Carla (Product): Quick sync — NovumHealth pilot asked for 100ms p50 SLA on hosted+private hybrid with HSM-backed keys. Need a concrete scope decision today: do we (A) add HSM + dedicated pool for pilot, or (B) ship hosted fallback with stricter data retention and 150ms p50?
Mike (Runtime): 100ms p50 for their seq lengths is... ambitious. We can try prefix caching + aggressive batching but that pushes infra requirements. Rough ETA: ~2 weeks to validate on a canary rig.
Srini (Eng-Infra): If we go dedicated pool we need reservation for 4x A100-equivalents for the pilot window. That’s a monthly commit unless we do burst VMs. Cost + procurement lead ~3w.
Elaine (Security): HSM integration adds a KMS policy + audit log pipeline change. Also need vendor attestation for on-prem HSM. Minimum runway ~2 weeks for policy + 1 security review.
Jason (PM): Can we list minimal launch criteria so we can negotiate scope with Novum? I think: 1) data encryption at rest with customer-managed keys, 2) pilot SLA p50 target, 3) rollback/fallback path, 4) audit logs available.
Carla (Product): Yup. If HSM blocks, fallback must be: hosted model with envelope keys + guaranteed 90d log retention and an explicit SLA of 150ms p50. Customer prefers HSM but accepts fallback if we sign SSO + contract terms.
Mike (Runtime): Realistically to hit 150ms p50 we can enable per-tenant KV caching + int8 quantization on the model artifact. That’s one small model build + runtime flag flip. We can do that in ~5 business days for a single model.
Srini (Eng-Infra): For prod-like latency we should pre-warm a dedicated node pool and pin the model shard. If infra provides burst-only (no commit) we can still prewarm but risk evictions during load.
Elaine (Security): Note: customer requires HSM key wrap for private artifacts. If we use envelope keys on hosted, contract needs explicit allowed-use clauses. I can draft the wording but need legal loop.
Carla (Product): Ok trade-offs: Ship faster with hosted fallback (150ms) or longer runway for HSM + 100ms. Which is lower-risk for us?
Mike (Runtime): Lower engineering risk: hosted fallback with caching+quant => 150ms. Lower customer confidence risk: HSM path.
Srini (Eng-Infra): Operational risk: committed capacity buys reliability. Burst capacity is cheaper but higher outage risk.
Jason (PM): Proposal: Offer Novum a two-phase pilot. Phase 1 (2 weeks): hosted fallback with caching + 150ms SLA publically measured. Phase 2 (4–6 weeks): optional HSM + dedicated pool with 100ms SLA if they sign reserved capacity. Present that as timeline + costs.
Carla (Product): I like that. Action items: Mike — validate caching+quant perf on sample traffic (ETA 5d). Srini — cost estimate for 4x reserved nodes vs burst prewarm (ETA 3d). Elaine — draft HSM KLAs + security checklist (ETA 3d). Jason — pricing & contract sketch for reserved capacity (ETA 2d).
Mike (Runtime): Starting a perf run now. Will post logs.
deploy-bot: Deploy queued: canary-runtime-v2 to perf-rig at 1719980321
Mike (Runtime): Perf run logs: `p50=142ms, p95=310ms` on current rig with caching enabled. Baseline model still FP16. Int8 quantizing may shave another 20-30ms.
Carla (Product): Good data, thanks. Jason — can you share the two-phase plan with Novum and ask if they can commit to reserved capacity for Phase 2?
Jason (PM): Will do. I’ll ping legal and sales for contract KPs.
Carla (Product): Final: schedule a 30m handshake next Tue 10am to sign off on action items. If anyone needs an earlier sync, ping me. :white_check_mark:
Elaine (Security): Noted. I’ll include the audit log retention SKUs we need.
Srini (Eng-Infra): I'll include cost + lead time matrix.
Mike (Runtime): Will post final perf numbers before EOD Friday.
Carla (Product): Thanks all — keeping this thread as single source of truth for Novum pilot scope/sequence.
